security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU emulates a trap taken on interrupt i into level x under Smnip and sets {xithreshold} to iprio[i] (the priority of the incoming interrupt) rather than the current IPRIO (the active interrupt priority before trap entry). If the previous threshold was already elevated above iprio[i] (e.g., a higher-priority interrupt was being serviced), this incorrectly lowers the threshold, allowing lower-priority interrupts to preempt the handler.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: xithreshold = iprio[interrupt_id] or xithreshold = interrupt_priority (value derived from the triggering interrupt, not from the current IPRIO CSR field) during trap entry in ACLIC/Smnip interrupt handling path
security_spec.summary: Smnip trap entry must set xithreshold to IPRIO (current priority level) not iprio[i] (incoming interrupt priority) — using iprio[i] incorrectly resets threshold to the incoming interrupt's priority, allowing lower-priority interrupt preemption when threshold was already higher

findings.finding: Smnip extension and xithreshold CSR are not implemented in this QEMU codebase. The trap entry function riscv_cpu_do_interrupt() contains no xithreshold-setting logic, no IPRIO capture into xpistatus.pithreshold, and no xithreshold restore in xRET. There is no ext_smnip feature flag, no xithreshold/xpistatus CSR definitions, and no ACLIC emulation. The vulnerability described in the security spec (xithreshold incorrectly set to iprio[i] of the incoming interrupt rather than current IPRIO during trap entry) cannot manifest because the feature is absent.

spec_citations.excerpt: The existing trap behavior is modified as follows: When a trap is taken into level x, the current value of xithreshold is written to xpistatus.pithreshold. Additionally, if the trap was taken on an interrupt, xithreshold is set to IPRIO. This automatically raises the interrupt-enable threshold. If a double trap occurs while in M-mode, xpistatus.pithreshold is unchanged. NOTE: Synchronous exceptions do not modify the value of xithreshold.

findings.finding: The PR adds a MENVCFG_CDE check before allowing scountinhibit access. This is an unrelated fix for the scountinhibit CSR — it does not involve Smnip, xithreshold, or interrupt priority thresholding.
The PR adds an IOMMU device context validation for MSI page table pointer mode when GATP is BARE. This change is unrelated to Smnip, xithreshold, or interrupt priority thresholding.
